paras: The killing of Boston Frederick took place in Campbell County, Georgia, near Fairburn, where a posse of citizens led by a deputy sheriff shot dead Frederick, a Black escaped convict, in August 1900. By the posse's account, he aimed a shotgun at them when they came to arrest him, and Georgia and Alabama papers reported the killing as a fugitive resisting arrest.

According to a Fairburn dispatch, Frederick had been indicted in February 1899 for arson in connection with the burning of Palmetto, but the bill was quashed. He was instead sent to the chaingang for 12 months for carrying concealed weapons, and after returning to the county he was sentenced to another 12 months for assault and battery. The dispatch said he escaped while serving that term in the employment of A. G. Orvin & Co. of South Georgia, came back to the county, and had been "swearing vengeance" on those involved in his convictions. The Savannah Morning News instead described him as having escaped from the chaingang "several weeks ago."

Sheriff Aderhold received a message from people near Frederick's hiding place asking him to come and make the arrest, and he directed a deputy to summon a posse. The posse found Frederick in the lower part of the county late on the afternoon of Wednesday, August 8. In the words of the dispatch, "he leveled a doublebarreled shotgun at them, and was instantly shot down." The Savannah report gave the same account, saying he "levelled a gun on the officer and posse."
No report of an inquest or of any inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage, and only the posse's version of events was printed.

The story ran in white papers on August 10 and 11, chiefly as a dispatch dated Fairburn, August 9. The Americus Times-Recorder printed the fullest version under the headline "Negro Slain by the Posse. Escaped Convict Resisted Arrest and Is Shot Down," calling Frederick "a negro of desperate character." The Birmingham Age-Herald carried a two-sentence form headed "Negro Killed by Officers." The Savannah Morning News ran a separately worded item, "Killed Fugitive Convict," naming Campbell County and calling him "a desperate negro."
All three papers presented the posse's version as fact and led with his criminal record; no report in the Black press was found.

reader.title: Killing of Boston Frederick
bases: A posse of citizens led by a deputy sheriff, sent to arrest an escaped convict, shot him dead when, by their account, he aimed a shotgun at them (A1, A3).

Frederick was killed by a group, but the papers describe a posse summoned on the sheriff's orders and led by a deputy attempting a lawful arrest, who fired when he resisted (A1, A3); the only account is the officers' side, and no report shows an extralegal purpose.

The Fairburn dispatch (A1, A2) and the separately worded Savannah report (A3) agree that a deputy-led posse killed Frederick while trying to arrest him, though all versions give only the officers' account.
